open_obligations: Check which assumptions (rho-stability, A-provability) prover-estimator debate adds relative to doubly-efficient debate.
Check whether the guarantees shift from deterministic worst-case to average-case.
Verify the cost comparison assumes q constant and q^d = O(n^c).

in.other_title: Prover-estimator debate mitigates the obfuscated arguments problem in recursive debate
in.rationale: Brown-Cohen, Irving and Piliouras introduce doubly-efficient debate, in which two polynomial-time provers compete so that, under appropriate assumptions, any polynomial-time computation can be verified with a constant number of human-judgement queries. Brown-Cohen et al. (2025) propose a new recursive debate protocol that, under stability assumptions, keeps the honest debater's required efficiency comparable to its opponent's while addressing the obfuscated arguments problem that affects existing recursive protocols. Both ask whether debate can work with efficient debaters, in different settings.
in.scope: proposed SAME_QUESTION_DIFFERENT_SETTING: whether debate can be made to work with efficient debaters, in doubly-efficient debate (two polynomial-time provers, a constant number of human-judgement queries, under appropriate assumptions) and in recursive debate facing obfuscated arguments (an honest debater that wins with efficiency comparable to its opponent, under stability assumptions)

text: The authors introduce doubly-efficient debate, in which two polynomial-time provers compete to convince a much more efficient verifier of the correctness of a computation that depends on black-box access to human judgements. They prove that, under appropriate assumptions, any polynomial-time computation can be verified using only a constant number of queries to the black box representing human judgement, in time linear in the size of a single query.
title: Doubly-efficient debate: poly-time honest prover, constant human-judgement queries
